message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command that brings up the Docker daemon – it only starts an existing container. If you want to bring the Docker service (the engine that runs containers) up on Windows, you have two common ways: | What you want | How to do it | |---------------|--------------| | **Start the Docker Desktop GUI** (recommended for most users) | 1. Make sure Docker Desktop is installed.
2. Run the executable:
`Start-Process 'C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe'`
(or just double‑click the Docker Desktop icon). | | **Start the Docker Engine service from PowerShell/Command Prompt** | 1. Open PowerShell **as Administrator**.
2. Run one of the following:
* `Start-Service Docker`
* `net start com.docker.service`
(Both commands start the same Windows service that hosts the Docker daemon.) | ### Quick one‑liner (PowerShell) ```powershell Start-Service Docker # or net start com.docker.service ``` ### Quick one‑liner (Command Prompt) ```cmd net start com.docker.service ``` > **Tip:** If you’re using Docker Desktop, the service name is `com.docker.service`. If you installed Docker Engine via the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) or a custom setup, the service name may differ; check `Get-Service` in PowerShell to list available services. --- #### Starting a Container If you actually meant to start a **container** after the engine is running, you would use: ```bash docker start ``` Replace `` with the name or ID of the container you wish to start. --- **Summary** - `docker start` → starts a container. - `Start-Service Docker` or `net start com.docker.service` → starts the Docker daemon/service on Windows.
